subject: zoology
question_text: What are the excretory cells of flatworms called? What is the other important function of these specialized cells?

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.53, VSAQ 91). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The excretory cells
steps.why: The name records what is seen down a microscope, a moving tuft of cilia, so the structure and the name are learnt together.
common_mistakes: Calling them nephridia. Nephridia belong to annelids; flatworms have protonephridia built from flame cells.
Writing that flame cells are found in roundworms. They belong to the flatworms.
steps.memory_tip: Flat worm, flame cell. The tuft of cilia inside is the flame.
steps.margin_note: Give the name, then one line on what the cell looks like.

steps.label: The other function
steps.why: A flatworm has no other route by which water can leave the body, so the same cilia that drive out the waste also drive out the extra water.
common_mistakes: Writing respiration as the second function. Flatworms exchange gases through the body surface.
Answering only 'excretion'. The question asks for the OTHER function.
steps.memory_tip: Two jobs, one cell: waste out and water balance.
steps.margin_note: Name the second function and say in one line what it means.
lines: Besides excretion, flame cells carry out
They drive out the excess water and keep the
amount of water and salts in the body steady.
